# Large encrypted RAR regression provenance

`tools/encrypted_rar_psd_smoke.py` creates its fixtures under the selected output's `encrypted-rar-psd-cases` folder. The source repository contains the small generator and this note, never generated large files, user artwork or a RAR writer.

The original synthetic PSDs reuse the large raw-layer layout from `large_archive_psd_smoke.py`, with **512×384 saved composites**. Each source exceeds 512 MiB because of a 14,000×13,000 raw zero-filled layer. Image A has a warm orange corner marker and red/green gradient; image B has a blue corner marker and green/blue gradient. Different saved colors make stale-source errors visible. The package also includes the repository's existing tiny `image.png` under `small-seed.png` for navigation-test setup.

Archives are created by an **independently supplied official RAR CLI**, not by custom cryptographic code. The test uses RAR5, compression method 1, a 1 MiB dictionary, one thread and non-solid files. `-p` encrypts file data; `-hp` also encrypts file names and headers. Every archive is tested with the separately bundled 7-Zip reader before the viewer runs. The [RARLAB format documentation](https://www.rarlab.com/technote.htm) describes RAR5 encryption; command semantics are checked against the supplied official `Rar.txt`/`Rar.exe -?` help.

The test distinguishes **large extracted entries** from **large physical ciphertext archives**. The two method-1 archives compress the synthetic zero-filled layers to small containers. Separate method-0 stored archives, `large-stored-data.rar` and `large-stored-headers.rar`, each contain `large-a.psd` and the seed, and must physically exceed 512 MiB before testing proceeds. Container byte sizes are recorded independently from entry sizes. The compressed archives used by the same-Viewer navigation test are never rewritten while adding the stored variants.

For the recorded local test, the root agent acquired official **RAR 7.23** from [RARLAB](https://www.rarlab.com/rar/winrar-x64-723.exe), verified its Authenticode signature and extracted the CLI without installation. Installer SHA256: `8ff0daf3ed564cc743c0e23ff2e253997ffc74460f9673f0b6dd037b2db4ce7b`; `Rar.exe` SHA256: `f561764bc3e9ed208744321a89a819b562edeaf06e203c02a06976121fda1991`. RAR is proprietary evaluation software with its own license; it remains in ignored test output and is not distributed with RustView. Other users must supply a CLI they are licensed to use. The only password accepted by this generator is the public fixture value `fixture-password`; it never ingests or records a user's real archive password.

The tests cover missing/wrong/correct passwords, indexing, full-size viewing, 128-pixel thumbnails, single composite-page handling, PNG16 exports and repeated cancellation/reload. Unencrypted file names in `-p` archives can be listed without a password; this must not be confused with authenticating the file contents. A per-request `TEMP`/`TMP` directory is checked independently of process cleanup. The test samples its own probe descendants with [Toolhelp snapshots](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/tlhelp32/nf-tlhelp32-createtoolhelp32snapshot), holds process handles, and verifies their termination with [WaitForSingleObject](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/synchapi/nf-synchapi-waitforsingleobject). An unrelated RustView GUI is excluded. All observed descendants must exit, and the longer-running 7-Zip process must be observed for decode/cancel cases; very short-lived subprocesses can fall between samples.

Descendant attribution also checks process creation times against the held parent's lifetime. A historical parent PID alone is insufficient: Windows can reuse that PID while an old child still exists. Memory sampling uses the same verified process handles. Run `python tools/encrypted_rar_psd_smoke.py --tracker-self-test` for the lifetime-boundary checks.

Cancellation is tested at 300 ms during repeated reloads and at 150 ms for early extraction. Early-cancel cases require a nonzero, incomplete `input.psd` observation, a real `已取消` supervisor result, all observed PIDs terminated and an empty request-temporary directory. The trace records whether the selected entry was partly or completely spooled when cancellation occurred; later cancellation is not described as partial extraction. An earlier 500 ms test could race with successful completion; the tighter deadline requires an actual cancellation rather than treating legitimate completion as an application failure.

Memory measurements are sampled private committed bytes for the probe and its descendants, excluding the Python harness and reclaimable OS file cache. Repeated CLI requests exercise real supervisor/worker cancellation and cleanup, but do **not** establish same-Viewer GUI navigation behavior or long-run cache stability. Those need the separate navigation probe or GUI acceptance.

`tools/navigation_smoke.py --exe <RustView.exe> --fixtures <encrypted-rar-psd-cases> --output <report.json>` runs eight same-Viewer checks through the normal binary's `--navigation-probe` route. The application uses the real navigation handlers, pending/running queue, stale-generation filtering, drawing and supervised decoding; no native window or filmstrip worker is created in this probe. Intervals are 10 ms and 250 ms. Compressed cases end on the distinct second large PSD; physical stored cases switch between their single large PSD and the small seed. Pixel oracles are loaded independently and do not pre-populate the Viewer's cache.

Every case captures a live partial extraction, cancels by navigating, checks the final target and pixel digest, then starts another real partial extraction and requests window closure. It verifies resource retirement and temporary cleanup before Close, and feeds the next Close event back through the handler to require the absence of CancelClose. This models the pinned eframe close-event semantics; native-window keyboard and shutdown acceptance is recorded separately. The live spool-size observer uses an opened file handle, since Windows directory-enumeration metadata can lag ongoing writes.
